stories.headline: U.S. strikes Iran and Tehran fires back as hostilities flare again
stories.deck: Iran’s military warns of ‘devastating blows’ as country reports attack on airport Strikes have renewed after Iran said it would stick to a ceasefire deal if the US did the same
stories.bodyText:
The U.S. military hit targets in Iran on Tuesday (September 1, 2026), and Tehran fired missiles and drones in response as hostilities flare once again in an intermittent war that has lasted more than six months.
The U.S. strikes followed others on Sunday that abruptly ended a month without military action and threatened to fully reignite a conflict that has spiked global oil prices and posed political problems for Republicans in November’s midterm congressional elections. The renewed fighting comes after President Donald Trump had appeared to pivot toward trying to bend Iran to his will through economic sanctions.
“If the failed Nation of Iran retaliates for this very justified attack, they will be hit again at a much harder and higher level, but it will not be the biggest attack of them all, that is waiting in the wings,” Mr. Trump warned on social media.
U.S. Central Command said the latest strikes were in response to Tehran trying to attack commercial ships and American forces in the Middle East. Trump offered an additional explanation, telling Fox News in a phone call that U.S. forces struck Iran’s radars.
“They tried to rebuild their radar because they can’t see anything,” Mr. Trump told Fox. “We waited until it was almost built and then we hit it.”
Iranian state media reported that the U.S. had bombed civilian sites along Iran’s southern coast and hit a civilian airport. A U.S. strike hit a home where a wedding ceremony was being held in Kuhestak in southern Iran, killing two people and wounding at least 20 others, Ahmad Nafisi, Hormozgan Province’s deputy governor, told Iranian state television in a phone call.
Iran’s Armed Forces General Staff and its joint military command said the armed forces would deliver what they described as “crushing and devastating blows” against the United States. The state-run IRNA news agency cited a statement by Iran’s paramilitary Revolutionary Guard, which warned that the attacks have only strengthened the Islamic Republic’s resolve and tightened Iran’s effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, through which 20% of the world’s oil normally flows.
Explosions were reported across several southern Iranian coastal areas, including the port city of Bandar Abbas that is home to naval and air force facilities as well as Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. Witnesses in Bandar Abbas told The Associated Press that the explosions were stronger than those on Sunday and said they saw smoke rising from the eastern part of the city on the strait.
Iranian state television said U.S. strikes hit a fishmeal factory on Qeshm Island and several civilian sites in Hormozgan province. It said a fishing pier and a Ports and Maritime Organization tower in Sirik were among the locations struck.
State TV also reported that the U.S. military struck the civilian Jiroft Airport in central Iran’s Kerman province, saying a projectile struck an area outside the runway and caused no casualties or damage to airport infrastructure. U.S. Central Command did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment on those reports.
The U.S. and Iran are both seeking control over the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow waterway off Iran’s coast that is a vital oil shipping corridor. Tehran effectively closed it after the war began.
Oil prices have moved sharply higher this week with renewed clashes between Iran and the United States. Crude, already up about 7% this week, continued to rise following the strikes on Tuesday.
The price of crude has jumped more than 50% this year and it’s dragged the cost of gasoline upward with it. The cost for a gallon of regular gasoline in the U.S. ticked higher again overnight to $4.10, according to AAA. Last year at this time, a gallon cost $3.19.
Before military action began again, the Trump administration had argued that hitting the right economic target in a campaign of financial isolation would get Tehran to its breaking point. Now, strikes are renewing even as U.S. stockpiles of advanced interceptors have been diminishing and the war has been unpopular among many Americans.
A return to open conflict would be dangerous for the region, where Iran has targeted U.S. military bases and infrastructure in Gulf countries since the war began.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said earlier Tuesday before the latest strikes that the Islamic Republic is ready to return to the interim ceasefire deal reached with the U.S. in June if Washington does the same.
“If the U.S. returns to its commitments in the memorandum of understanding, the Islamic Republic of Iran will immediately reciprocate,” Iranian state media cited Pezeshkian as saying at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Kyrgyzstan.
The June interim deal called for an immediate ceasefire and started a 60-day period for negotiations aimed at reaching a wider agreement, but crumbled soon afterward.
In the previous strikes on Sunday, U.S. Central Command said its forces struck Iranian rocket launchers that would launch sea mines into the strait.
Iran responded to Sunday’s attacks by launching missiles at U.S. sites in Jordan, which were intercepted, while United Arab Emirates said it stopped an Iranian drone over its waters. Trump acknowledged Monday that more strikes might be necessary.
The American military in recent days has cast the renewed fighting as limited, though Trump had acknowledged Monday that more strikes might be necessary.
U.S. Central Command said Monday on X that its attacks on Iranian targets on Sunday were narrowly focused.
“U. S. forces took limited, precise action against IRGC minelaying forces posing an imminent threat in the Strait of Hormuz,” U.S. Central Command said. “In essence, Iran created the threat and the U.S. military eliminated it to protect civilian mariners, commercial shipping, and the free flow of global commerce.”
Central Command reiterated Tuesday that its attacks followed Iranian aggression against commercial vessels and American troops in the region.

stories.headline: Nepal flash floods aftermath LIVE: Death toll crosses 1,000 as rescuers recover more bodies; nearly 4,000 still missing
stories.deck: Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah said that the devastating flood that entered Rasuwa was due to climate change
stories.bodyText:
The death toll from the devastating flash floods in Nepal surged to 1,050 on Tuesday (September 1, 2026), with security forces recovering more bodies from eight districts of the country, officials said. Nearly 4,000 people, including 583 foreigners and 83 security personnel, still remain missing the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) said.
Watch | How a school in Nepal saved 900 students from a devastating flash flood
Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah, meanwhile, said that the devastating flood that entered Rasuwa through the Bhotekoshi River bordering Tibet last week was due to climate change. Mr. Shah further said that climate change is a global contribution and disaster response remains a global responsibility.
Nepal disaster, a grim reminder to rethink preparedness | Data
The number of Indian nationals rescued in the wake of the devastating flash floods in Nepal stands at 163, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, as India sustained its relief and rescue efforts in coordination with Nepalese authorities. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal also said a 19-member specialised forensics team from India that began functioning in Kathmandu on Sunday (August 30), as well as a tunnel rescue team deployed in Nepal in a statement shared along with the post.

stories.headline: Zelenskyy says Ukrainian drones have effectively closed Russian airspace
stories.bodyText: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned airlines and insurance companies on Tuesday that the presence of Ukrainian drones had made Russian skies dangerous to use and were effectively closed."Today, we want to warn every airline that uses Russian airspace, every insurer, everyone who still uses key Russian airports: the Russian sky is becoming completely dangerous," Zelenskyy said in his nightly video address.Ukraine poses no threat to civil aviation, he said, "but there will be drones in Russia's skies and due notice must be taken"..Indian killed in Russian attacks in Ukraine after PM Modi's 'end of war' call to Putin."Although Russian authorities are not properly announcing it, Russian airspace will effectively be closing. The war started by Russia is closing its own skies," Zelenskyy added.Russia has stepped up its air attacks on Kyiv and other cities in recent weeks, with Moscow's latest strike killing 12 people and injuring many more, the sixth straight day of intense assaults on the Ukrainian capital.Ukraine has responded with frequent drone strikes on Russian targets, many associated with the country's oil industry as well as retail sites.

stories.headline: CJP hails Supreme Court order quashing protest FIRs, says compensation policy must reach NEET victims' families
stories.bodyText: New Delhi: The CJP on Tuesday termed the Supreme Court's decision to quash FIRs registered against NEET protesters a "major victory" and said the government's commitment to frame a pan-India compensation policy within three months must now translate into relief for affected families..The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) said in a statement that the court's order provided relief to protesters who faced criminal cases for participating in the demonstrations over the NEET-UG paper leak crisis, including unidentified persons, and would also cover any similar FIRs subsequently found to have been left out of the lists submitted by the Centre and states.."Today's decision is a victory for every student who was told that raising their voice was a crime. We protested because the government refused to listen. Instead of answering students, the state responded with FIRs and police action," CJP founder and national convenor Abhijeet Dipke said..The Supreme Court has now given relief to those who were "dragged into criminal cases for exercising their democratic right to protest", he said, adding that the ruling should send a message that dissent cannot be suppressed through intimidation.."Students should be in classrooms, not police stations. They should not have to take to the streets to demand basic accountability from their government. This decision should be a lesson to those in power that dissent cannot be silenced through intimidation," he said..The CJP also welcomed the Supreme Court taking note of the government's commitment to formulate a pan-India compensation policy within three months for families of students who died by suicide in connection with the NEET-UG paper leak crisis..CJP co-convenor Saurav Das said the commitment was significant for families that had been seeking recognition, accountability and financial support.."There is no compensation for the loss of a child. Nothing can undo what these families have gone through. But the government cannot look away from its responsibility," Das said.."The commitment made before the Supreme Court must now translate into a fair and transparent policy that reaches every eligible family," he said..Supreme Court acquits ex-bank manager, brands CBI loan case ‘fabricated’.Das said the families had already waited long enough and should not have to continue fighting for recognition and relief..Das, in a post on X later, said more than 130 FIRs had been quashed by the Supreme Court and described the order as a "big win" for the younger generation. He said the court had also recorded that states and Union territories would not register fresh FIRs against protesters or target them in the future for their participation in the protests..Das said the court had agreed to extend the relief to any FIRs subsequently found to have been omitted from the lists submitted by the Centre and states. He described the protection for unidentified protesters as particularly significant, saying the order was perhaps the first such "John Doe"-like quashing order by the Supreme Court..On compensation, Das said the CJP had agreed to a three-month timeline for the government to provide relief to families of students who died by suicide in connection with the NEET-UG paper leak crisis. He said the organisation would continue to monitor implementation of the commitment..Separately, CJP leaders have begun reaching out to families of students who died in connection with the examination crisis, it said in a statement..Dipke spoke to the families of several victims, while co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka visited the family of Pradeep Meghwal in Sikar, Rajasthan..The organisation said it would continue engaging with affected families and follow up on the compensation process to ensure they do not have to navigate it alone..The CJP has also said it would monitor the implementation of the Supreme Court's directions and the government's three-month commitment on compensation, while the September 5 march announced by the organisation had been called off..The apex court quashed all FIRs registered against students who participated in the CJP-led protests across the country between July 20 and 25 and said the cases should not affect their future. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant also directed the Centre to provide within three months compensation to families of students who ended their lives over the NEET paper leak..Acceding to the Centre's request, the court, however, permitted Delhi Police to register fresh FIRs against 2,873 individuals with serious criminal antecedents who were present at the Jantar Mantar protest.

stories.headline: Ram temple cash theft: Journalist accuses cops of digital tracking
stories.bodyText:
Abhishek Upadhyay, the journalist who reported embezzlement of donations at Ayodhya's Ram temple, on Tuesday sought Supreme Court's intervention saying that Ghaziabad police have, in connection with a case of road rage against him, sought his digital footprints from social media platform X since June 1, which could jeopardise identities of sources who tipped him about the donation scam.
His counsel Anoop P Awasthi told a bench led by CJI Surya Kant that Ghaziabad police's request to X HQ in California for the alleged road rage case of Aug 18 would result in gross violation of his right to privacy, adding that such data in the hands of police would reveal the identities of the sources who informed him about temple theft.
The FIR concerns an alleged incident of Aug 18, yet the investigating agency seeks the petitioner's IP and account-related information from June 1, well before the alleged incident. No nexus between such sweeping historical digital information and the investigation of the alleged incident has been disclosed in the impugned notice," Upadhyay said in his application.
The bench said it had on Aug 25 protected the journalist from coercive action by police in the road rage case and that his fresh application would be listed for hearing in due course.

briefs.headline: Three candidates shortlisted for Ram Janmabhoomi Trust’s first CEO
briefs.deck: The Trust is expected to choose one of the three at a meeting on September 2; names of the shortlisted candidates have not been disclosed, but sources said the panel includes candidates from government and private sectors
briefs.bodyText:
New Delhi
The search committee constituted to select the first Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust (SRJTKT) has shortlisted three candidates and submitted their names to the Trust, the committee said on Tuesday (September 1, 2026).
The Trust, which oversees the Ram temple in Ayodhya, is expected to choose one of the three candidates at a meeting on Wednesday (September 2, 2026).
The decision to appoint a CEO came amid the controversy over alleged theft and irregularities in the handling of donations at the temple. Following the embezzlement allegations, SRJTKT general secretary Champat Rai and trustee Anil Mishra resigned.
On July 6, the trust announced a major administrative overhaul, including the creation of the CEO post. The move was aimed at strengthening administrative oversight and restoring confidence in the trust’s functioning.
“The trust was also considering changes to its bylaws to formally provide for a CEO and clearly define supervisory responsibilities, particularly in relation to fund management,” a source close to the selection committee informed.
Selection process
To select the CEO, a three-member committee was formed comprising retired Justice Pramod Kohli, retired Lieutenant General V.K. Chaturvedi and scientist Dr. Suresh Haware.
The selection process began in July after the committee finalised the eligibility criteria, which included experience in temple administration and being a “staunch Hindu”. Applications were closed on July 18, following which online interviews were held in early August. Sixteen candidates were subsequently called to Ayodhya for in-person interactions on August 11 and 12.
“A total of 5,585 applications were screened using AI-assisted tools as well as manual review,” said search committee secretary Sameer Panda. The evaluation was conducted by teams based in Delhi-NCR, Pune and Sambalpur in Odisha, Mr. Panda said.
The names of the shortlisted candidates have not been disclosed, but sources said the panel includes candidates from government and private sectors. The three names have not been placed in any order of preference.
The committee’s final report was presented at a meeting attended by trust treasurer Swami Govind Dev Giri, Mahant Dinendra Das, acting general secretary Krishna Mohan and Ayodhya District Magistrate Shashank Tripathi.

briefs.headline: CJP chief hails Supreme Court's quashing of FIRs against students
briefs.deck: Abhijeet Dipke says justice has been dispensed to all those who fought at Jantar Mantar, and to the families of those who died due to NEET paper leak
briefs.bodyText:
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) welcomed the Supreme Court's move to quash all FIRs registered against students who participated in the NEET protests across the country, calling it "absolute justice".
Talking to reporters here, Mr. Dipke thanked the court and said justice had been dispensed to all those who fought at Jantar Mantar and to the families of those who died do to NEET paper leak.
The Supreme Court on Tuesday (September 1) quashed all First Information Reports (FIRs) registered against students who participated in the CJP-led protests between July 20 and 25 across the country. A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant also directed the Centre to provide within three months compensation to families of students who ended their lives over the NEET paper leak.
"Our demands have been met. This is absolute justice. It took us a month [for this]," Mr. Dipke said.
He said this was made possible due to people's power, adding that he had been holding meetings with several delegations on the issue.
"I apologise to the families that we could not save your kids. We are very sorry that you lost your kids," the CJP convener said, referring to those who lost their loved ones and blamed the government for its failure.
The students lost their lives because of the government's failure, he alleged, and said the government had also accepted that it would provide compensation to the families of students who died.
"The government has accepted the demands, but it has to take responsibility that not a single student dies due to paper leak," the CJP convener said.
Mr. Dipke further added that the government must ensure that no student loses life due to failure of the system.
"We cannot afford this anymore," he said.
The CJP-led march on July 20 in Delhi saw clashes between protesters and security personnel, who used lathis and tear gas shells to disperse crowds attempting to move towards Parliament.
The student-led protests, which spread to several cities, were centred around the resignation of the then Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
The agitation, which began at Jantar Mantar on June 20, was called off on July 25 after Mr. Pradhan resigned and the government accepted the CJP's other demands.

briefs.headline: World War II: The unsung role of India and its soldiers in the global conflict
briefs.deck: Although the Indian Army fielded the largest volunteer force and fought on battlefields across the globe, there is little by way of a comprehensive archive documenting its experiences
briefs.bodyText:
The years spanning the Second World War, from Germany’s invasion of Poland on September 1, 1939, to Japan’s surrender on September 2, 1945, remain etched in history as a global conflict that lasted six years and involved millions of people across four continents. Approximately 85 million people lost their lives, most of them civilians, due to mass killings, genocide, starvation, and disease
World War II, which also bears the grim distinction of being the only conflict in which nuclear weapons were used, was fought between the Axis powers, principally Nazi Germany, Italy and Imperial Japan, and the Allied powers, including Great Britain, the Soviet Union, the United States, France and China.
Also read | When the world went to war
India’s forgotten history
In India, memories of the war have largely receded from public consciousness, as the years between 1939 and 1945 are remembered chiefly as the closing phase of the struggle for Independence.
Although the Indian Army fielded the largest volunteer force and fought on battlefields across Africa, Europe and Asia, there is little by way of a comprehensive archive documenting its experiences. Britain, the United States and France have fared better, with museums and archival institutions ensuring that the memories and lessons of war are preserved.
Also read | Remembering the war, reminiscing forgotten Indians
Between war and nationalism
India’s reticence towards the two World Wars stems from the uneasy relationship between its contribution to the fight against fascism abroad and the nationalist movement at home. The success of the former is often viewed as having come at the expense of the latter. The roots of this perception lie in the dashed expectations of greater autonomy after India supported Britain during the First World War.
Britain had already alienated many Indian nationalists through the imposition of martial law after the First World War, culminating in the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in April 1919. Matters were further complicated when Viceroy Lord Linlithgow declared war on Germany on India’s behalf in 1939 without consulting Indian leaders. The situation became even more contentious when Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose’s Indian National Army aligned itself with the Axis powers in the belief that doing so could hasten India’s freedom.
India’s pivotal role in World War II
India raised the largest volunteer Army in history for the Second World War, with 2.5 million men serving. More than 87,000 of them are buried or commemorated in war cemeteries in India and abroad. Soldiers from undivided India were awarded 31 Victoria Crosses, accounting for about 15% of all such honours conferred during the conflict.
Also read | The guns at last light
Field Marshal Claude Auchinleck, Britain’s last Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Army, acknowledged years later that without Indian soldiers, non-combatant labourers, material resources and financial support, the course of both World Wars might have been very different.
Beyond a distant war
More than 1,61,000 personnel laid down their lives in the two World Wars. Yet the prevailing perception is that these were wars fought for someone else and in distant lands. As a result, India’s substantial contribution has often been marginalised in historical narratives.
But these were not just European wars to defend foreign lands. During the Second World War, Japanese forces advanced through Burma, now Myanmar, posing a direct threat to India. Their advance was halted at the battles of Imphal and Kohima between March and July 1944.
Indians fought not only across South Asia but also in several parts of Africa, Europe and the West Asia. India also served as a crucial geographical barrier between Imperial Japan and Nazi Germany, preventing the two Axis powers from linking up through the West Asia. Maintaining this separation was vital to the success of the Allies in the war. Had Germany and Japan been able to coordinate their campaigns more closely and gain access to the oil resources of the West Asia, the balance of the war could have shifted dramatically in favour of the Axis powers.
Also read | Retracing Chennai’s role in the Second World War
World War II in Visakhapatnam
Although the Second World War began in Europe in 1939, by early 1942 it had spread deep into Asia as Japanese forces advanced through Malaya, Singapore and Burma (now Myanmar). British authorities feared that India’s eastern coastline could become vulnerable to attack. Visakhapatnam, with its harbour and strategic position along the east coast, quickly assumed military significance. Historian and chronicler Edward Paul, who has extensively documented the city’s wartime history, notes that fears of a Japanese occupation had a profound impact on both the administration and residents.
Those fears materialised on April 6, 1942. That morning, Cocanada, now Kakinada, was bombed by a lone single-engine aircraft, becoming the first town in India to be attacked from the air. Journalist, author and former Editor of The Hindu Mukund Padmanabhan records this in his 2024 book, The Great Flap of 1942: How the Raj Panicked Over a Japanese Non-invasion. Visakhapatnam was bombed three times on the same day and suffered far greater damage.
Published - September 02, 2026 06:39 am IST

briefs.headline: Congress attacks BJP over exclusion of over 2 crore voters in Maharashtra SIR
briefs.deck: Congress said that in West Bengal, 91% of the voter names struck off in the SIR had to be reinstated after appeals
briefs.bodyText:
Flagging the exclusion of 2.06 crore names in Maharashtra’s draft electoral rolls after the special intensive revision (SIR), the Congress on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) said votes were being added and deleted to ensure that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) wins elections.
The deletions in Maharashtra, where draft rolls were published on Monday (August 31), are the largest in absolute numbers for any State in the ongoing Phase 3 of the SIR.
Following the 2024 Maharashtra elections, the Congress had formally submitted representations to the Election Commission alleging large-scale voter roll manipulation, including unusual voter spikes in several constituencies. It had alleged that forged documentation, such as fake Aadhaar cards with mismatched names and photos, were used to add fictitious voters without physical verification of addresses.
On Tuesday (September 1, 2026), Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said “the BJP and the ‘vote theft commission’ keep changing their tactics, and they will continue to do so; the goal remains just one: BJP’s victory at any cost, and the end of India’s democracy”.
In a post on X, he said: “Maharashtra 2024 - Suddenly, 3.9 million new voters were added between the Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha elections. I said it then, and I say it today: This was vote theft.”
“And now in Maharashtra, 2.07 crore voters have been removed from the draft list — that’s every fifth voter. Lok Sabha 2024: 9.29 crore, Vidhan Sabha 2024: 9.7 crore, SIR 2026: 7.78 crore. Which list was correct,” Mr. Gandhi asked.
“For a government built on vote theft, the people are not important—that’s why this BJP neither listens to the people nor obeys their command,” he added.
Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge said votes are added when it suits the BJP. “Where it doesn’t, votes are split to perpetrate vote theft,” he said.
“The BJP’s conspiracy to hollow out Indian democracy by stealing votes is coming out into the open. Instead of acting as the guardian of fair elections, the Election Commission is functioning like the “Save BJP’s Chair Commission,” he wrote on X.
Both leaders said that in West Bengal, 91% of the voter names struck off in the SIR had to be reinstated after appeals. “That means 9 out of every 10 names were wrongly deleted, and added back only after the election. I said it then, and I say it today: This was vote theft”, Mr. Gandhi said.
Mr. Kharge said that the “same game” was being repeated in Delhi. “Voters were increased before the Assembly elections, then names of 4.756 million voters vanished from the draft list, and preparations are underway to issue notices to 3.3 million other voters,” he said.
He said that in Telangana and Karnataka, Congress workers faced similar manipulations every day. “The country is now uniting against vote theft. The nation has understood the BJP’s conspiracy, the thief has been caught. Punishment will surely be meted out for holding democracy captive,” he added.
The Election Commission, meanwhile, has shared figures showing that 3,35,910 booth-level agents appointed by different recognised political parties were engaged in preparing the draft electoral roll for Maharashtra, and another 33,226 for Delhi.
Published - September 01, 2026 08:36 pm IST

briefs.headline: Putin says Zelenskyy's threat to close Russian airspace is 'state terrorism', Moscow will respond
Putin seeks to end Ukraine conflict; open for talks
briefs.deck: The Russian president acknowledged that Ukrainian attacks inside Russia had inflicted real damage and stated that drones posed a particular challenge
briefs.bodyText:
President Vladimir Putin said on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) that Russia was winning the war in Ukraine and portrayed the Ukrainian leadership as “terrorists” with whom it was not possible for Moscow to negotiate.
Mr. Putin, in his most detailed comments on the war for many weeks, acknowledged that Ukrainian attacks inside Russia had inflicted real damage and said that drones posed a particular challenge.
But he said that Russia was advancing on the battlefield and told reporters, “I have no doubt the enemy will crumble.”
He declined to say when that would happen.
Rumours that Russia would be forced to order a new military mobilisation were “utter nonsense”, he said.
Russian troops had captured 270 square km (168 square miles) of the Donetsk region in eastern Ukraine in August, and a large group of Ukrainian troops were surrounded, Putin said.
Reuters could not independently verify his statement.
Russia continues to advance towards the cities of Sloviansk and Kramatorsk, Mr. Putin said, adding that Moscow’s forces were preparing to launch massive strikes against energy infrastructure in Ukraine.
Mr. Putin said that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s warning to airlines that Ukrainian drones would effectively shut down Russian airspace sounded like “state terrorism” and that Moscow would find a way to respond if it happened.
Speaking at a news conference after a summit in Kyrgyzstan, Mr. Putin said it was not possible to negotiate with “terrorists”.
He also said, however, that Moscow was open to “concrete” talks on settling the Ukraine conflict if new momentum could be injected.
Published - September 02, 2026 06:43 am IST

briefs.headline: Nepal flash floods aftermath updates: PM Shah links devastating floods to climate change as death toll crosses 1,050
briefs.deck: Around 4,000 people remain missing, while nearly 12,000 have been rescued
briefs.bodyText:
Devastating floods on the China-Nepal border have killed at least 1,050 people in Nepal, the disaster authority said on Tuesday (September 1, 2026), with nearly 4,000 more missing. Security forces are recovering more bodies from eight districts of the country, officials said. Around 4,000 people remain missing, while nearly 12,000 have been rescued, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) said.
ALSO READ | Nepal disaster, a grim reminder to rethink preparedness | Data
Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah on Tuesday said that the devastating flood that entered Rasuwa through the Bhotekoshi River bordering Tibet last week was due to climate change.
“There is no doubt that climate change has caused this disaster, as it has been confirmed that the temperature in the Himalayan region has increased by 1.8 degrees,” he said in a post on social media.
ALSO READ | The Bhotekoshi flood | A Himalayan tragedy
Flash floods, triggered by a collapse or avalanche of ice and rock near the Nepal-Tibet border, devastated towns and villages in northern and central Nepal on August 26. The Bhotekoshi River, which flows south from the Himalayan border region, carried the floodwaters downstream, sweeping away homes, vehicles, roads and bridges and damaging hydropower projects.
As many as 321 bodies were recovered in Chitwan district, followed by 216 in Nawalparasi East, 170 in Nawalparasi West, 95 in Nuwakot, 65 in Gorkha, 57 in Dhading, 41 in Rasuwa and 38 in Tanahun, according to NDRRMA.

stories.headline: Flyover or slowover? Bengaluru’s new traffic rules are here
stories.bodyText:
What happened?
Bengaluru’s flyovers are about to get a little more selective.
From September 4, traffic police will introduce vehicle restrictions on five major flyovers and elevated corridors across the city, in a move aimed at improving road safety and easing congestion. The changes will affect the BOS flyover, Peenya elevated corridor, Double-Decker flyover and International Airport flyover, while restrictions on the Electronic City elevated corridor will kick in from September 11.
The rules have sparked plenty of conversation among Bengalureans. While some commuters are welcoming the move in the hope of smoother and safer journeys, others are wondering if keeping certain vehicles off flyovers will really make a dent in the city’s larger traffic woes.
The big question, of course, is whether these new rules will finally make the commute a little easier—or simply move Bengaluru’s traffic jams from one road to another.
The new flyover rules:BGS flyover:
Heavy goods vehicles will be prohibited. Light goods vehicles will not be allowed between 7 am and 11 am, and between 4 pm and 10 pm.
Peenya elevated corridor: Passenger and goods autorickshaws will be completely prohibited. 
Heavy and medium goods vehicles will be restricted between 7 am and 11 am, and 4 pm and 10 pm.
International Airport flyover:
 Two-wheelers and autorickshaws will be barred. All goods vehicles will face restrictions between 6 am and 10 pm.
Double-Decker flyover:
 Heavy goods vehicles will be completely prohibited.
Electronic City elevated corridor:
 Goods vehicles will be banned between 6 am and 10 pm. Two-wheelers and autorickshaws will be completely barred.
Compiled by Mehwash Hussain

stories.headline: Three wheels, no shortcuts: Autorickshaw driver puts Karnataka on Ladakh map
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 At a time when many auto drivers in Bengaluru refuse to travel from one part of the city to another citing long distances, 35-year-old Balakrishna Mohan decided to take his auto much farther — all the way to Ladakh. Over 24 days, he covered approximately 7,500km, climbed some of the region’s highest passes and reached Umling La, one of the highest motorable stretches in the world at 19,024ft.
“I used to see videos of different types of vehicles, including autos from other states, at Umling La. I wanted to represent 
Karnataka
,” he said. He claims his is the first autorickshaw from Bengaluru to reach Umling La and return home.
Balakrishna spent a few weeks preparing for the journey. He sold his auto and bought a second-hand one, changing its registration plate from yellow to white as it was meant for private use. He decided against modifications, having already taken a loan and wanting to avoid unnecessary expenses. With a tent, sleeping bag and other essentials packed, he was flagged off by friends and well-wishers from Vidhana Soudha on Aug 1.
“I took the Hyderabad route. From there I went through Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, Agra, Jammu & Kashmir, and then to Leh,” he said. From Leh, he headed to Khardung La and planned to proceed to Nubra, but a landslip forced him to turn back. 
He then travelled to Pangong Lake and Chang La before proceeding to Hanle and finally Umling La.
“The moment I arrived there was one of the happiest moments of my life. I had never thought I would be able to do it in my autorickshaw,” he said. “On my way, I saw so many vehicles that had fallen in ditches and thought, ‘What am I doing?’ But somehow, my auto and I ended up climbing the pass.”
For Balakrishna, the expedition was also about putting Karnataka on the map. “Many there did not know about our state. It felt good to educate them about our wonderful state,” he said. He also scaled Chang La and Fotu La passes.
The adventure came with mishaps. Near Umling La, he lost his way in the rain and travelled 13km in the wrong direction, almost reaching a restricted border area, before locals helped him back. To save money, he had initially planned to pitch his tent at petrol pumps, but after encountering thieves, he switched to dormitories and hostels. Vehicle breakdowns were another challenge.
His auto runs on CNG, but from Jammu onwards he had to rely on petrol as there were no CNG stations along the route. He credited army personnel and fellow Kannadigas in Ladakh for helping him through difficult stretches.
“Our army personnel guided me everywhere, from navigation to helping me make the hardest turns. Any Kannadiga I met there also gave me their number and told me to contact them if I needed help,” he said.
Balakrishna Mohan, 35, the auto driver
On his way back, Balakrishna travelled through Himachal Pradesh, drove through the Atal Tunnel and reached Bengaluru on Aug 24, completing approximately 7,500km. “It was different from what I had imagined. If my health had permitted, I’d have even covered Kanyakumari and come,” he said.
Originally from Mysuru, Balakrishna lives in Sarjapur with his wife and two children. He has been driving autos since 2011 and hopes his adventures will inspire his children. His next adventure is already taking shape, and he hopes a philanthropist will help him undertake the journey.

stories.headline: Parks amendment bill can be discussed again in the Assembly: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar
stories.deck: Mr. Shivakumar says he will examine and discuss why the proposal to allow the use of 5% of park land was brought in, and also what the BJP and other previous governments had done.
stories.bodyText:
In what could be read as a note of reconciliation, following protests against the controversial amendment that allows alienation of up to 5% of park and garden land for public infrastructure in Karnataka, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) said the proposal could be reviewed and discussed again in the Karnataka Legislature Assembly.
The Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) (Amendment) Bill, 2026, was passed in both Houses of the Legislature on August 24, 2026, amid Opposition protests over the inclusion of B. Nagendra due to his alleged role in the embezzlement of funds in the Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribe Development Corporation.
The Bill aims to facilitate the tunnel road project to take over an acre of Lalbagh land, sources said. This has been followed by protests by environmental groups, citizen organisations and Bengaluru BJP MPs. Thousands of citizens gathered at Lalbagh on August 30 to protest against the amendment Bill.
The Chief Minister said that he would examine and discuss why the proposal to allow the use of 5% of park land was brought in, and also what BJP and other previous governments had done, and which land had been allotted to whom in the past.
“I will get the files and we can discuss the matter again in the Legislative Assembly,” he said. He added that the government would also review instances of land being provided for various purposes in Bengaluru, including the land provided from Lalbagh for the metro.
Responding to questions on the protection of park land, Mr. Shivakumar said, “No one needs to worry. I know how to protect the park land. The decision will be in public interest.”
Mr. Shivakumar said he was open to suggestions from the Opposition as well as the public.“I am open to the suggestions of the Opposition. I will also consider the suggestions of the public. My intention is not to create any confusion,” he said.

stories.headline: BDA offers sites in Dr. K. Shivaram Karanth Layout in Bengaluru at ₹6,000/sqft
stories.deck: Site prices have skyrocketed from ₹2000/sqft in NPKL to ₹6000/sqft in the Dr. K. Shivaram Karanth Layout
stories.bodyText:
After a gap of a decade, the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) on Monday, August 31, reopened its portal for applications for site allotment, this time in the much-awaited Dr. K. Shivaram Karanth Layout. The last time the BDA allotted sites was in Nadaprabhu Kempegowda Layout (NPKL) in July 2016.
Site prices have soared from ₹2,000 per sq. ft. in NPKL to ₹6,000 per sq. ft. in the Dr. K. Shivaram Karanth Layout. This means a 30x40 site, the most preferred by middle-class Bengalureans, will cost a whopping ₹72 lakh.
When the BDA first initiated the allotment process in the layout in December 2023, it had fixed the price at ₹4,900 per sq. ft. However, the process was stayed by the Karnataka High Court over the issue of compensation to land losers. In less than three years, the price has appreciated by ₹1,100 per sq. ft.
On July 16, the high court allowed BDA to invite and process applications for site allotment in the layout, based on which BDA has now opened the portal for receiving applications. However, the court said that the BDA cannot allot sites and that would depend on further directions issued by it.
The deadline for the process will be communicated soon, senior BDA officials confirmed to The Hindu.
Sites for landlosers
This came on a day when about 18,300 farmers who had given land for the layout, were allotted sites by Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar. The beneficiaries will now have to produce the necessary documents and complete the formalities to claim their sites.
BDA chairman N.A. Haris said the developed layout had achieved a yield of 55%, with 49.38% of the total developed land being returned to landowners as sites.
This is expected to clear the decks for allotment of sites to the general public.
Speaking after distributing the site allotment letters, the chief minister said that the government had been trying to distribute compensation for the past three years and had invited applications, but the process was delayed due to court proceedings. “A court stay had also delayed the process of inviting applications for site allotment, resulting in a loss of ₹1,000 crore to the government every year. The layout, spread across 3,700 acres, has seen an investment of ₹16,000 crore,” he said.
He further appealed to the farmers who were to receive sites in the layout as part of the compensation package not to sell them. He further said the government was also working on a revised compensation mechanism for farmers whose land was acquired for BDA projects.
“While the existing system required compensation based on old rates, the government had proposed providing twice the guidance value, double TDR, or 35% of the land as commercial sites, FAR or 40% of the developed land. “We have taken this to the Cabinet to ensure farmers are not treated unfairly. The highest compensation in the country has been provided,” he said.
Mr. Haris said the authority was relying heavily on technology to make the site allotment process transparent and prevent the involvement of brokers. He said a committee had been formed to look into the concerns raised by farmers, including demands for sites closer to their existing areas, issues concerning ancestral burial grounds and requests for specific locations for the developed sites.

briefs.headline: ‘Just let us build roads’: Commuters reach breaking point over civic apathy in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: After years of driving over potholes and broken stretches, and repeatedly watching freshly repaired roads fall apart, a north Bengaluru motorist says he has had enough. His latest demand to govt is as blunt as it is unusual: if you can’t build roads, give citizens permission to do the job.
Deepak Gowda
, a private firm employee, has taken to social media to highlight the poor condition of 100 Feet Road near Kanteerava Studio in Yeshwantpur. He has appealed to Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) to allow motorists to crowdfund and repair the damaged stretch, saying years of official inaction have left them with little choice.
“If you can’t build the road, just give us permission. We’ll fund it and build it ourselves. Just as we raise funds for Ganesha festival, we’ll collect money for road repairs. I’ll sponsor a tractor-load of gravel and the rental cost for an excavator (JCB machine),” he said in the video, which has struck a chord with frustrated commuters.
He said the road has been in poor condition for more than five years and deteriorated further after utility works dug up the stretch around three years ago. 
Repeated representations eventually led to the road being asphalted after the issue was taken up with the chief minister’s office. However, the relief was short-lived.
Within a few months, the newly laid road began deteriorating, leaving motorists back where they started — negotiating potholes and damaged stretches despite repeated complaints and repairs.
Large sections of the road now resemble a construction site rather than a city road, with open drains running alongside broken carriageways and leaving little safe space for pedestrians. Deep craters dot the stretch, forcing motorists to constantly swerve to avoid damaging their vehicles. Several potholes have been filled with construction debris instead of being properly repaired, making the surface even more uneven.
“So much tax is collected from people, and you cannot provide something as basic as a road. What are you there for?” he asked, slamming the civic authorities.
Large sections of 100 Feet Road near Kanteerava Studio in Yeshwantpur are riddled with craters, dust and open drains, making the stretch hazardous for motorists and pedestrians
During dry weather, thick clouds of dust engulf the stretch, reducing visibility and making every commute uncomfortable. Residents say the uneven surface, exposed drains, debris-filled potholes and dust have turned what should be a key arterial road into one of the area’s most hazardous stretches.
‘Tired of waiting’
What surprises him most is the response from fellow commuters. “Whenever I stop to click pictures of the road, people come up to me just to vent their frustration,” he told 
TOI
. “I have asked some if they would contribute money to fix the road, and almost everyone says yes. People are tired of waiting.”
Despite repeatedly writing to the CM’s office, elected representatives and officials, Deepak says his complaints are routinely closed without explanation. “We are in 2026 and still fighting for something as basic as a road in India’s technology capital. Why should citizens who pay taxes have to beg for basic infrastructure?” he asked.
For Deepak, the issue goes beyond potholes. He switched from a two-wheeler to a car to avoid the dust and diversions, but says he worries about pedestrians and bikers who continue to endure the daily ordeal. “At least level the road properly until it is asphalted. Instead, debris is dumped into potholes, making the road worse. We’re done. We’re simply done putting up with this kind of infrastructure,” he said.
His words may be directed at one road, but the sentiment extends far beyond Yeshwantpur, capturing the growing frustration of countless Bengaluru residents who feel abandoned by a system they believe has stopped listening.

briefs.headline: Facilities, fees fuel student discontent at two universities in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Discontent is brewing among students at two private universities in the city. Students living in S-Residences Hostel, Dayananda Sagar University (DSU) main campus, are protesting over inadequate facilities, while a section of students at St Joseph’s University (SJU) has raised concerns over convocation fee.
Students at S-Residences Hostel in DSU’s Harohalli campus have been complaining about inadequate basic amenities and poor hostel conditions for nearly a month. The complaints led to protests on Aug 26 and Aug 31.
Among the issues raised are unstable or non-functional Wi-Fi, frequent electricity fluctuations, lack of hot water during peak morning hours, poor-quality drinking water, inadequate cleaning, leaking or overflowing plumbing, mosquito-related hygiene concerns, malfunctioning lifts, and empty vending machines.
The protest followed repeated complaints to hostel authorities that students alleged had not resulted in effective action. “On Aug 26, a girl approached the warden around 9.30pm regarding the lack of hot water and was allegedly dismissed rudely. Other students joined her, and the situation developed into a larger protest involving 300-350 girls,” said a hostel resident.
“During the protest, the hostel management primarily focused on the girls being outside after the 9.30pm entry deadline, rather than addressing their complaints. 
Boys from the adjacent hostel later threw firecrackers and eggs towards the protesting girls, but the management did not take adequate action,” she added.
Students were subsequently told that some issues would be addressed by Aug 30, and the remaining ones gradually. However, with little change by Aug 31, another protest was held, this time involving both boys and girls.
Meanwhile, the DSU management told 
TOI
 that all the issues were being addressed. “The building is relatively new and the contractor was still getting things straight. We called for a meeting with representatives from all towers Tuesday. They raised their concerns and we are addressing each of them,” said a management representative.
On eggs being thrown at the protesters, the management said, “It has got nothing to do with the management. It was some boys from the boys’ hostel behind it. Our faculty team is already in conversation with the students. We’ll also identify the culprits using CCTV footage.”
Over Rs 5,000 for convocation
A group of SJU students has taken to social media to protest the convocation fee. According to them, the university has charged Rs 4,500 in addition to another Rs 600. “We are also disappointed that our parents are not being allowed for the convocation. It is a lifetime opportunity for us,” said the students.
The SJU administration said it has changed the rules and will allow parents to attend the convocation, scheduled for the last week of Sept. “It is a small group of 20 students from earlier batches who failed to pass and have been creating the issue on social media. Those from the current batch are fine. Meanwhile, there are costs associated with the convocation. Various types of certificates need to be issued, not just a convocation certificate. We’re providing snacks, attire etc.,” said the administration.

briefs.headline: Mother allegedly drowns four-month-old twins, attempts suicide in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: Four-month-old twin babies were found dead at their home in Vajarahalli, south Bengaluru, Tuesday, while their mother was found trying to end her life in the same room.
According to the complaint filed by the babies’ father, Ramalingappa, 50, a real estate businessman, his wife, Umadevi, 40, had been undergoing psychiatric treatment after allegedly showing unusual behaviour, following the birth of their daughters on May 5 through IVF treatment. The couple got married in 2002.
Ramalingappa said for one and a half month after the delivery, Umadevi had allegedly shown disinterest towards the children and said she wanted to be admitted to an ashram. She was subsequently taken for treatment at hospitals in Raghuvanahalli and Nimhans, where doctors reportedly attributed her behaviour to postpartum depression and hormonal imbalance following childbirth.
On Tuesday, Ramalingappa returned home around 2.45pm and found the door of a room locked. After forcing it open, he found Umadevi hanging from a dupatta and rescued her. The twins were found unconscious inside the same room. They were rushed to a private hospital, where doctors said they may have died due to drowning. The family suspects she drowned the babies in a bucket full of water.
Talaghattapura police have registered a case under BNS section 103 (punishment for murder).

briefs.headline: Encroachments from 1,225km of footpaths cleared in 2 months: Greater Bengaluru Authority
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Greater Bengaluru Authority’s (GBA) ‘Safe Footpaths’ drive, launched on July 1 to reclaim pedestrian space and remove encroachments, covered 1,225km of footpaths across the city’s five corporations till Aug 31.
The drive was scheduled to conclude by Aug-end, but the exercise has been extended until Sept 3. West and North corporations had recorded the highest coverage, with 280km and 275km, respectively, till Aug 31. Bengaluru Central corporation covered 246.8km, South 244km, and East 179.6km during the two-month period.
“The most effective outcome of this is that permanent encroachments by commercial establishments have been removed and the footpaths have been reclaimed. We must acknowledge this,” said Bengaluru North City Corporation (BNCC) commissioner Pommala Sunil Kumar, adding that BNCC covered another 20km on Sept 1 and the civic body would now focus on repeat offenders.
BNCC had set a target of covering 333km of footpaths, of which 32km falls under white-topping, bringing the effective target for the drive to 301km.
Kumar said the corporation’s earlier ‘Walkaluru’ initiative, under which officials walked around 50km of the city’s footpaths, had helped identify the extent of encroachments. “North corporation showed the way by walking on footpaths and clearing them for pedestrians,” he said.
He added that BNCC has also earmarked Rs 25 lakh per ward for footpath restoration. “Removing encroaching vendors was a huge task earlier. Now that there is political will, we’ve been able to do a lot of work,” he said.

briefs.headline: Able-bodied man must support wife after divorce: Karnataka high court
briefs.deck: Citing SC dictum, court upholds Rs 15L permanent alimony awarded to woman
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Relying on two 
Supreme Court
 judgments, Karnataka high court recently upheld a family court order directing a man to pay Rs 15 lakh as permanent alimony to his wife.
In the Reema Salkan vs Sumer Singh Salkan and Anju Garg and Others vs Deepak Kumar Garg cases, the apex court had observed that an able-bodied husband cannot avoid his responsibility to maintain his wife and must work to pay maintenance. It also said courts must strike a fair balance between competing considerations while determining maintenance, a high court division bench of Justice DK Singh and Justice H Shanthi Bhushan noted in an order passed on Aug 20.
In the case at hand, the couple got married on Feb 5, 2009. At the time, the husband was employed with the Central Manufacturing Technology Institute (CMTI), while the wife worked at a private establishment.
Their relationship turned sour within three months, following which the husband approached the Bengaluru family court seeking divorce. The court granted divorce on March 20, 2024, and also directed him to pay Rs 15 lakh as permanent alimony.
Challenging the alimony order, the husband argued that his wife had neither specifically sought permanent alimony nor produced evidence to support such a claim. He also contended that she earned Rs 30,000 a month, while he was already paying Rs 15,000 per month as maintenance.
The high court, however, found no grounds to interfere. It noted that the Supreme Court had issued guidelines requiring both parties to disclose their assets and liabilities so family courts could make a fair and realistic assessment of maintenance. However, these guidelines had not been followed in the present case.
The bench also rejected the husband’s contention that he had no source of income, observing that this, by itself, did not absolve an able-bodied and qualified man of his moral responsibility to maintain his wife.
The court noted that records showed the petitioner had been employed with CMTI, a govt undertaking under the ministry of heavy industries. Considering the financial circumstances of both parties and their standard of living, the family court had awarded Rs 15 lakh as permanent alimony to enable the wife to maintain herself with dignity and contribute towards the upbringing of their child, the bench observed.
The high court consequently dismissed the husband’s petition.

briefs.headline: Analyst at private firm arrested for running illegal hookah bar in Bengaluru
briefs.deck: He, along with another person, were allegedly running a hookah facility on the first floor of a house belonging to a person identified as Bhagyamma
briefs.bodyText:
An analyst working with a private firm in Bengaluru is among two men arrested for allegedly running a hookah bar illegally from a rented house in Kenchanapura village under Kumbalgodu police station limits.
One of the accused — Ajith Nayak, 28 — is a civil engineer working as a senior analyst in a firm, and the other — Varun K.R., 25 — is a service assistant.
According to Kumbalgodu police, they received credible information on August 31 that the duo had rented a house at Kenchanapura, and were operating a hookah facility.
Based on the information, police raided the house in the presence of witnesses. The accused were allegedly found running the hookah facility on the first floor of a house belonging to a person identified as Bhagyamma.
Police seized five hookah pots, three hookah pipes, two boxes of hookah pots, three used hookah flavours, partially used charcoal, and ₹450 in cash.
A case has been registered and further investigation is underway to ascertain whether others were involved. Police are probing the role, if any, of the house owner.

briefs.headline: More wards, same workforce: GBA, corporations struggle to deliver on the ground
briefs.deck: The State government replaced the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike Act, 2020, with the new Greater Bengaluru Governance Act, 2024, in 2025, which dissolved the BBMP and formed five corporations in its place, with a pan-city body called the GBA, which came into force on September 2, 2025
briefs.bodyText:
ONE YEAR OF GBA
Even as the five new corporations under the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) are close to completing a year since they were formed, old problems on the ground continue to haunt citizens, while they now seek a way out of new problems.
The State government replaced the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike Act, 2020, with the new Greater Bengaluru Governance Act, 2024, in 2025, which dissolved the BBMP and formed five corporations in its place, with a pan-city body called the GBA, which came into force on September 2, 2025.
The restructuring was envisaged to address micro-level issues through decentralisation of the administration. While the erstwhile Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) was split into five corporations, what mattered on the ground was that the number of wards in the city almost doubled from 198 to 369, which it was hoped would take the administration closer to citizens.
But this has made little difference on the ground. Even a year later, the city corporations are still mostly working with a workforce deployed for the old 198-ward setup and not upgraded to the 369 wards yet. Moreover, the vacancy rate is around 40%. This essentially means, the intended benefits of the new governance structure is yet to reach citizens.
R. Rajagopalan, convenor of Bengaluru Coalition, puts it this way: the GBA is like a novel concept on paper without an execution plan.
With the change in wards from 198 to 369, citizens struggle to find the engineers in charge of their wards, which forces them to visit corporation offices even for minor inconveniences.
Sneha Nandihal, co-founder, I Change Indiranagar, said there is still confusion about how the new system works. “All our engineers have dual charges, and when we question them about anything, they very conveniently say that they are just in-charge of specific work and get away. The accountability is missing,” she stressed.
Pranith B., a resident of Koramangala, pointed out that in the past, engineers would often visit their wards and ward committee meetings used to take place. “Now, once the complaint is raised, as they don’t visit often, follow-up becomes very hard, and repeated calls won’t yield a response. While many could get their issues resolved by visiting corporation offices, for the working class and labour class, accessing basic amenities has become hard,” he said.
V. Ramprasad, a solid waste management expert, pointed out that addressing the garbage issue needs micro-level planning, which requires a ward-wise blueprint. “At present, such planning has taken a hit with the dearth of engineers. Right from collecting waste to monitoring blackspots, we need sustained efforts, but staff shortage doesn’t allow such focus,” he said.
No space for experimentation
The commissioners, who spoke on condition of anonymity, admitted that the shortage forces them to curtail their ambitious plans and stick to managing everyday crises rather than experimenting with new solutions to existing problems.
“At their disposal, each officer is executing tasks meant for two or three officers. There has been no compromise in managing everyday issues, but existing staff is overwhelmed and there is less scope for collaborative experimentation,” a commissioner said.
For example, an official pointed out the reduction of congestion at the Kaggadasapura Railway Crossing in east Bengaluru following a new traffic model devised by the east city corporation and said, “Such micro-level issues are what was envisioned to be solved through restructuring. But in reality, there are only a few examples like that in the past year to show because the required strength is not available.”
Delay in new rules
The State government has been working on a dedicated Cadre and Recruitment (C&R) Rules for the GBA, but is yet to notify them a year after the authority was formed. Once the new C&R Rules are adopted, it is expected that the government will directly recruit more people for the GBA.
M. Maheshwar Rao, Chief Commissioner of GBA, told The Hindu that new C&R rules have been framed by a committee headed by former Chief Secretary T.M. Vijay Bhaskar and have been sent to the government for approval. “Initially, ground-level requirements were assessed and sent to the government, but we were asked to rework. Then the committee was set up, and recently it gave a report,” Mr. Rao said.
(This is the first of a series of reports evaluating the restructuring of Bengaluru governance, with GBA and five corporations, a year after the reform)

briefs.headline: Bengaluru’s new wards run on an old service network
briefs.deck: While 171 new wards were added to the civic map, there has been no corresponding expansion of facilities such as primary health centres, Indira Canteens or even ward offices
briefs.bodyText:
Let alone a primary healthcare centre or access to an Indira Canteen for an affordable meal, several facilities residents would expect to be situated closer to home, such as ward offices where they can report civic issues, are missing in the wards added to Bengaluru over the past year.
The Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA), which completed a year after replacing the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) with five city corporations, increased the number of wards from 198 to 369. But while 171 new wards were added to the civic map, there has been no corresponding expansion of facilities such as primary health centres (PHCs), Indira Canteens or even ward offices, the local touchpoints through which the five-corporation system was expected to bring civic services closer to residents.
No land, human resources
Officials acknowledge that such facilities would eventually have to come up closer to residents, but say the lack of government land and human resources has made expansion difficult.
K.V. Rajendra, West Corporation Commissioner, said the number of wards may have increased substantially, but the physical geography of the city has remained the same. “There are enough Indira Canteens and PHCs for the corporation. However, even if there is a need, we cannot have more because there is no government land available for such a facility. Hence, the emphasis is on maintaining and improving the existing facilities,” he said.
The same problem, he argued, is affecting plans to set up ward offices. While the corporation intends to increase their number and appoint ward engineers so that issues such as khata-related work, civic grievances and other local-body matters can be reported and addressed locally, identifying land or buildings for the offices remains a hurdle.
Across the five corporations, officials said there are plans to set up ward offices, but none of these plans has yet translated into offices on the ground. Apart from finding land for these facilities, filling vacant posts is another challenge, they say.
Even the focus of the corporations’ maiden budgets, meanwhile, has largely been on maintaining and upgrading the existing network, with allocations for disease control, food quality and other improvements, but no clear ward-wise expansion of facilities to match the increase in wards.
Gaps persist
Although the lack of expansion remains a question, even the existing PHCs and Indira Canteens continue to have gaps in accessibility and functioning.
Several PHCs remain difficult to locate, with shopkeepers and even residents in neighbouring areas sometimes unaware of their location or whether they are functioning. Some are also not readily available on online maps. For patients who do reach them, long waiting times, limited operating hours and inadequate availability of medicines are among the common complaints.
While PHCs are officially supposed to function from 9 a.m. to 4.30 p.m., at several facilities visited by The Hindu in Sultanpalya in R.T. Nagar, Vasanth Nagar and Rajajinagar, most staff had left by 4 p.m. Patients said the timings should either be extended or, at the very least, staff should remain until the official closing time.
Officials at these PHCs said the availability of medicines had improved, but shortages remained. Staff shortage is another challenge, they said. “The shortage becomes particularly apparent when patient footfall increases during seasonal changes like the rainy season. During such periods, the staff have to attend to a larger number of patients while also ensuring that pregnant women, senior citizens and others who cannot wait for long are attended to promptly, making the shortage more difficult to manage,” an official said.
Some PHCs and Indira Canteens, however, have seen visible improvements. For instance, PHCs in Agrahara and Amruthahalli have been painted with heat-reflective paint to reduce indoor temperatures and improve comfort for patients.
The experience at Indira Canteens, however, also varies considerably by location. While canteens such as those at Airport and J.C. Nagar, Vasanth Nagar, are maintained well, others, particularly those with lower footfall, are not run as efficiently or maintained as regularly, consumers said.
“A facility intended to improve food security by providing an affordable and dignified meal may naturally have lower footfall in some locations, but that does not necessarily make the need for the facility any less important,” said Thousif Aziz, an auto driver, pointing to an Indira Canteen in Majestic. The canteen, he said, is hemmed in by a heap of garbage on one side and a bus stand on the other, leaving little space around it.
(This is the second in a series of reports evaluating the restructuring of Bengaluru governance with the GBA and five corporations, a year after the reform.)

stories.headline: 5-member NCLT bench stays Subhash Chandra '6.5cr repayment order
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) on Tuesday stayed its earlier order allowing Zee Group founder Subhash Chandra to settle his personal insolvency proceedings by paying Rs 6.25 crore as against admitted claims of Rs 22,006.57 crore and also restrained him from alienating his assets. A five-member special bench headed by tribunal chief Anupinder Singh Grewal said there was no clear majority view on the repayment plan and put on hold the earlier order.
The litigation has remained inconclusive over the last one year because of dissenting orders. A two-member NCLT bench had delivered a split verdict in Sept 2025, with one member approving the repayment plan while the other rejected it, citing irregularities in the admission of claims and voting.
The case was referred to a third member, who on Aug 25 approved the repayment plan, subject to exclusion of certain disputed claims and reallocation of their share among eligible creditors. But the third member’s order was then found to have not produced a clear majority when read with the earlier split verdict, and this led to the constitution of the five-member special bench.
Analysing all three orders passed by different members, the five-member bench said, “It is manifest that as per Section 419 (5) of the Companies Act, 2013, there is no clear majority view capable of being given effect to; therefore, the order dated Aug 25 of the third member Nilesh Sharma, member (judicial), is stayed. 
We also direct that the personal guarantor shall not alienate any assets whatsoever either directly or indirectly. Let notice be issued to the parties in all the IAs (interim applications). Reply, if any, may be filed before the next date of hearing.” The tribunal posted the case for hearing after three weeks on Sept 23.
The dispute has also reached NCLAT, where dissenting lenders have challenged the repayment plan and the solicitor general sought a day’s time to decide whether the lenders wanted to proceed with the appeal.

stories.headline: Sun Pharma offers US cheaper drug supply
stories.bodyText:
New Delhi: Facing the threat of potential tariffs, India’s largest drug firm, 
Sun Pharma
 has offered Most Favoured Nation (MFN) pricing to US Medicaid programme under an agreement with the Trump administration. MFN pricing typically ensures that a buyer procures at the lowest price, compared to other developed nations.
The deal provides a playbook for domestic pharma companies looking to expand their sales in the US, the world’s largest market, by building their portfolio of innovative or speciality drugs. The agreement signed on Aug 31 recognises Sun Pharma’s investment in the US market by delaying potential Section 232 tariffs on innovative pharmaceutical products for over two years, a company statement said.
Under Section 232, US announced a 100% duty on innovative, patented drug imports, while generic medicines imported into the country would face tariffs of 100% from Aug 2028 and 200% a year later. The agreement with the US govt is aimed at prioritising access to affordable medicines for American patients.
US is Sun Pharma’s largest market for innovative medicines and a cornerstone of its long-term growth strategy, generating approximately 27% of its global revenue. 
Sun Pharma scrip closed over 1% lower at Rs 1,931 on BSE.
Analysts said sales of Sun Pharma’s innovative drugs in US are around $1 billion, and are expected to increase to about $3 billion, following acquisition of Organon.
“The agreement is a politically astute decision that needed to be made, while it also removes the overhang of tariffs. With the Organon deal, the company’s scale would increase significantly. There would be hardly any impact on earnings due to the reduction in prices’’, Vishal Manchanda, analyst at Systematix Group told TOI.
The development comes at an important time as the company continues to shift its US business beyond generics towards higher-value specialty and innovative medicines. Sun Pharma initially built its US presence on generics, followed by an increasing emphasis on innovative and specialty medicines. The company ranks second by prescriptions in US dermatology and continues to expand across dermatology and immunology, cutaneous oncology and ophthalmology.
The company joined eight pharma majors, which signed agreements on Aug 31 at the White House to reduce prices on drugs that treat numerous costly, chronic and even rare diseases, including hemophilia, Parkinson’s disease, macular degeneration, glaucoma, liver disease, skin conditions, and various forms of cancer, according to a White House statement.
Rick Ascroft, North America CEO, Sun Pharma, who represented the company at the White House, said: “The United States is a key area of investment and expansion for Sun Pharma across clinical development, sales and marketing, and both active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and finished products manufacturing’’. Further terms of the agreements remain confidential.
The agreement also includes a commitment to strengthen the US supply chain by contributing APIs to the Strategic Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients Reserve (SAPIR) to reduce reliance on foreign nations and ensure the US builds a stockpile. Sun Pharma will contribute 71.4 tons of clindamycin and 6.8 tons of doxycycline; both antibiotics to treat bacterial infections, to the SAPIR. The latest agreements bring the total number of pharma manufacturers with MFN deals to 26, covering 89% of branded drug market in the US.

stories.headline: Endurance test: On the Indian economy’s resilience
stories.deck: The quarters ahead will test the stamina of India’s economic resilience
stories.bodyText:
India’s economic growth during the first quarter of this financial year has surprised most people. Against a perception among economists that growth would slow to about 6%-7% on account of the impact of the West Asia crisis, real growth in the April-June 2026 quarter came in at a robust 7.8%. This was not a statistical anomaly, either, as growth was underpinned by strong performances in both manufacturing and services. In fact, the manufacturing sector grew at a three-quarter-high of 9.2%. The sector has likely benefited from the Goods and Services Tax rate cut implemented last September, and further from the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) 125-basis point cumulative interest rate cuts through 2025. A part of it is also that companies likely front-loaded their output in the expectation of further uncertainty on inflation, potential future rate hikes, and other possible headwinds. The other piece of good news is that capital creation seems to have picked up. While it is not yet clear what the share is between the government and the private sector, capital creation overall has a welcome multiplier effect on the economy. The services sector, too, has continued to see robust growth, adding strength to the economy. Yet, the economy is not out of the woods, and this robust performance will be more difficult to replicate in the quarters ahead. As Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran has cautioned, Hormuz uncertainty is likely to keep oil prices above $80 a barrel, too high for a country that imports 85%-90% of its oil requirement.
This is perhaps why Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday reiterated his appeal to Indians to buy local, avoid non-essential foreign travel and weddings abroad, and stop unnecessary purchases of gold. The pressure of maintaining a reasonable trade deficit has so far rested on India’s services exports. This has served India reasonably well so far, but the global economy is stuttering. This, combined with the growth of Artificial Intelligence services elsewhere, could hurt demand for Indian services exports going ahead. The economy is also yet to face the full brunt of a deficient monsoon and the impact this will have on rural demand. The consumption-related data for July in the Index of Industrial Production already points to sluggish rural demand. While inflation remains well within the RBI’s comfort zone, it has been increasing. The RBI expects it to hit 5.9% in October-December 2026, which would further hit demand. The front-loading of manufacturing will also, by definition, peter out over the next few quarters. The strength of the Indian economy’s resilience was tested in Q1 and it passed admirably. However, the much tougher stamina test remains.

briefs.headline: TCS pips Accenture to take over Best Buy's India GCC ops
briefs.deck: Five-Year Deal Size Estimated At 2k Cr, To Deepen Cos' Ties
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Indian IT firms are stepping up their global capability centre (GCC) playbook. TCS pulled ahead of Accenture in the final leg of the race to take over the India GCC operations of US consumer electronics retailer Best Buy, people familiar with the matter told TOI.
Best Buy floated a request for proposal (RFP) for a technology services engagement, and TCS won the mandate based on competitive pricing and aggressive service-level agreements (SLAs) and productivity benefits, sources said. Wipro is learnt to have been part of the initial shortlist.
Best Buy's India GCC, based in Bengaluru, has around 600 employees. The five-year deal, covering the GCC operations and broader technology services offering, including data, analytics and AI, is estimated to be worth around Rs 2,000 crore, people in the know said. Emails sent to TCS, Accenture, Wipro and Best Buy did not elicit a response till press time.
The deal would deepen TCS's longstanding relationship with Best Buy, spanning technology services and digital transformation. Phil Fersht, CEO of HFS Research, estimated the existing TCS relationship with Best Buy at $75-$100 million in annual revenue, while stressing that there is no publicly disclosed contract value.
Best Buy set up a 70,000-sft technology centre in Bengaluru in 2024 to accelerate its digital transformation. The centre was envisaged as an innovation hub spanning digital strategy, product management, design, engineering, infrastructure and operations.
"It's our intention to really make the Best Buy India hub the heart of innovation around how we're going to use mobile and AI platforms. We're going to be building and ramping up teams very actively in those areas," Brian Tilzer, then chief digital, analytics and technology officer at Best Buy, had told TOI in 2024.
The India centre has become more strategic as Best Buy steps up investments in AI and digital commerce. The retailer reported revenue of $41.7 billion in FY2026, compared with $41.5 billion a year earlier, while comparable sales rose 0.5%. Computing and mobile phones drove growth, partly offset by declines in home theatre and appliances.
