briefs.headline: Rs 25,000 salary to Rs 1 crore EPF corpus: Compounding math can make you a crorepati
briefs.deck: Over time, the interest earned on the accumulated balance earns interest, allowing compounding to steadily increase your retirement savings. With regular contributions maintained over a long period, an employee can potentially build an EPF corpus of Rs 1 crore or more.
briefs.bodyText:
Being a crorepati and accumulating a corpus of over Rs 1 crore is often a financial goal for money. But when you are thinking of SIPs, mutual funds, stock markets, ETFs, gold, silver, one quiet savings instrument may lead you to the coveted gold, building a crore plus corpus in less than 30 years.
The Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF) serves as a long-term savings avenue, helping employees build a retirement corpus through regular contributions and the power of compounding. Contributions are made by both the employee and employer, subject to the applicable EPF rules.
As an employee’s salary grows during their working life, the amount going towards EPF can also rise from the minimum monthly contribution of Rs 1,800.
EPF math: How compounding can take you past Rs 1 crore
Over time, the interest earned on the accumulated balance earns interest, allowing compounding to steadily increase your retirement savings. With regular contributions maintained over a long period, an employee can potentially build an EPF corpus of Rs 1 crore or more.
Of course, the time required to accumulate a Rs 1 crore through EPF depends largely on the monthly contribution and the number of years for which the money remains invested.
A longer contribution period gives compounding more time to work, meaning even smaller regular contributions can eventually grow into a substantial corpus. Similarly, higher contributions from the employee and employer can help build a sizable retirement fund over a shorter period.
To see how an EPF corpus of Rs 1 crore could be accumulated, consider an employee with a basic salary of Rs 25,000 a month. For the purpose of this calculation based on SBI Securities calculator, the employee’s EPF contribution is taken as 12% of basic wages. That calculator assumes an employer contribution to EPF at 3.67% since out of the employer’s 12% contribution, 8.33% goes towards the Employee Pension Scheme Account.
The calculation can then show how long it could take to reach the Rs 1 crore mark.
Under these assumptions, the employee could accumulate approximately Rs 1 crore in around 29 years. While the government reviews the EPF interest rate annually, in this calculation we are assuming that the rate remains unchanged at 8.25% throughout the period. We have also assumed an average 6% annual increase in salary, which in turn would increase your EPF contribution every year.
Every contribution made to EPF continues to earn interest during the investment period. As the employee’s salary increases, the contributions made by both the employee and employer also rise.
As a result, the amount added to the EPF account changes from year to year rather than remaining the same throughout the 29-year period.
Under these assumptions, the employee’s total EPF contribution would amount to around Rs 34.61 lakh, while the interest accumulated over the period would be approximately Rs 66.85 lakh. Combined, the contributions and interest would result in a retirement corpus of over Rs 1 crore, according to the SBI Securities calculator.
The final amount in the EPF account can, however, vary depending on factors such as the employee’s actual salary, annual salary increases, contribution levels, periods without employment, the employer’s contribution and the EPF interest rate applicable during the 29-year period.
Maintaining a 6% annual increase in basic salary over several decades can make a substantial difference to the eventual corpus. If the salary rises at a higher or lower rate, the corresponding EPF contributions and the final retirement corpus would also change.
Also, if you start at a basic salary of Rs 25,000 at the age of say 22, the final corpus at the time of retirement would be much higher. The 29 year period is the time it would take for your EPF corpus to cross the Rs 1 crore mark with all conditions mentioned above staying the same.
Can an employer deduct its own EPF contribution from an employee’s wages? No. An employer is not permitted to recover its share of EPF contribution by deducting the amount from an employee’s wages. Such a deduction constitutes a criminal offence, according to an ET report.
Can an employee contribute more than the statutory EPF rate of 12%? Yes. In addition to the mandatory contribution, an EPF member can make voluntary contributions.
(Disclaimer: Times of India does not give any personal finance or stock market investment advice. Always consult an expert before taking investment decisions)

briefs.headline: Bank employees to go on indefinite strike demanding five-day work week
briefs.deck: Union leaders say promises made by the government and bank managements in 2024 had not yet been implemented
briefs.bodyText:
Seven unions of bank employees, under the banner of the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU), have announced an indefinite strike from October 26, 2026, raising a four-point charter of demands, including the implementation of five-day banking, a promise made to them in 2024.
Talking to reporters here on Tuesday (September 1, 2026), UFBU leaders said that as part of their agitation, all-India bank strikes would be held on September 11, September 28, September 29 and September 30, as well as a "continuous, indefinite" strike starting October 26 if the demands are not met.
Maintaining that the unions were forced to undertake the agitation due to the actions of the government and bank managements, the UFBU leaders said the promises made to them were not implemented.
According to them, in an agreement signed in March 2024, bank managements had agreed that Saturdays would be declared holidays and unions had agreed that working hours would be increased by 40 minutes from Monday to Friday. "This agreement has been recommended to the Finance Ministry, Government of India, for their approval. It has been more than two years now, but the issue is still pending with the Finance Ministry," UFBU leaders said.
They also urged the Union government to withdraw the “unilateral and discriminatory” performance-linked incentive scheme, prescribed by the Union Department of Financial Services (DFS). They said the cost of the Incentive paid to 5% of the staff is far more than the total Incentive paid to the other 95% of staff, which they alleged was resulting in huge discrimination.
“Many of them have not been paid any incentive at all,” union leaders said, adding that the DFS’s scheme is contrary to the mutually and bilaterally agreed uniform scheme. “The DFS scheme seeks to divide the composite team of the workforce in the banks, who are today working as a unified team to achieve the targets and business parameters," they said.

briefs.headline: Sun Pharma agrees to supply at MFN pricing to U.S. medicaid programmes
briefs.deck: The U.S. is the company’s largest market for innovative medicines and a cornerstone of its long-term growth strategy, generating approximately 27% of the company’s global revenue.
briefs.bodyText:
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries will extend Most Favoured Nation (MFN) pricing to state medicaid programmes of the U.S. It has also committed to MFN pricing for future innovative medicine launches.
The announcement followed a White House ceremony on August 31, in which the U.S. government signed agreements with nine pharmaceutical companies, including Sun Pharma, aimed at improving access to affordable medicines for millions of Americans.
Sun Pharma said the agreement recognises its investment in the U.S. market by delaying Section 232 tariffs on innovative pharmaceutical products for over two years. Further terms of the agreements remain confidential, the company said.
“The United States is a key area of investment and expansion for Sun Pharma across clinical development, sales and marketing, and both API and finished products manufacturing. We are proud to play our part in delivering the medicines that millions of American patients count on every day,” said Rick Ascroft, North America CEO, Sun Pharma, who represented the company at the White House.
The company said it built its U.S. presence on a foundation of high-quality generic medicines, followed by an increasing focus on innovative and specialty products. It ranks second in the U.S. by prescriptions in dermatology and continues to expand its presence across dermatology and immunology, cutaneous oncology, and ophthalmology. These businesses complement its strong portfolio of consumer health products and generics.
The U.S. is the company’s largest market for innovative medicines and a cornerstone of its long-term growth strategy, generating approximately 27% of the company’s global revenue. Earlier this year, Sun Pharma signed a definitive agreement to acquire Organon & Co in a deal valued at $11.75 billion.
The White House said the nine new agreements are part of President Donald Trump’s initative to lower prescription drug prices for Americans in line with the lowest prices paid by other developed nations (known most-favoured-nation price). With the latest agreements, 26 pharmaceutical manufacturers now have signed MFN deals, covering 89% of the branded drug market.
Alcon, Astellas Pharma, BeOne Medicines, BridgeBio, CSL, Kyowa Kirin, Sun Pharma, Teva Pharmaceuticals, and UCB are the nine manufacturers.
The agreements will provide every State Medicaid programme in the country access to MFN drug prices on products made by the nine companies, resulting in billions of dollars in savings for Americans.
The nine manufacturers have committed to invest at least $19.6 billion collectively in U.S. manufacturing in the near term. Additionally, as part of the agreements, several companies are donating active pharmaceutical ingredients for key products to the Strategic Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients Reserve (SAPIR) to reduce reliance on foreign nations and ensure the U.S. has an adequate supply of such products in the event of an emergency, the White House said.
Sun Pharma will contribute 71.4 tonnes of clindamycin and 6.75 tonnes of doxycycline -- both antibiotics -- to the SAPIR.
Medicaid is jointly funded by States and the federal government in the U.S. and provides health coverage to millions of Americans, including eligible low-income adults, children, pregnant women, elderly adults and people with disabilities.

briefs.headline: Commercial LPG prices hiked by around ₹10 per cylinder, aviation fuel by ₹6.28/litre
briefs.deck: Prices of the free-trade 5-kg cylinders were also increased by approximately ₹2 per cylinder. The price of domestic cylinders remained unchanged.
briefs.bodyText:
Reversing course after two months of decline, prices of the commercial variant of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) cylinders were hiked by approximately ₹10 per cylinder across the country on Tuesday (September 1, 2026). The price of domestic cylinders remained unchanged.
Prices of the free-trade 5-kg cylinders, which cater largely to the migrant populations, were also increased by approximately ₹2 per cylinder.
Other than LPG, the prices of aviation turbine fuel (ATF) for domestic airlines were also increased to ₹121.28/litre, a hike of ₹6.28 per litre.
Prices in metro cities
The latest hike brings the price of the 19-kg cylinder in Delhi to ₹2,747.5 per cylinder, following a ₹9.5 hike. In Mumbai, they cost ₹2,701 per cylinder following a similar hike. In Mumbai, they cost ₹2,701 per cylinder following a ₹9.5 hike. Among the metro cities, Kolkata observed a steeper hike, with the commercial cylinder price rising by ₹11.5 to ₹2,884. In Chennai, the price rose to ₹2,916.5 per cylinder, an increase of ₹10.5.
The 5-kg free-trade LPG cylinders now cost ₹764 per cylinder in the national capital. Sales of free-trade LPG cylinders have recently seen an uptick, with new LPG connections on hold amid supply uncertainties due to the re-escalation of the conflict in West Asia.
Offsetting impact
According to Prashant Vashisht, senior vice president and co-group head, corporate sector ratings, at ratings agency ICRA, the latest commercial LPG price hike primarily seeks to somewhat offset the under-recoveries being incurred on domestic LPG cylinders.
“At present, the under-recovery on domestic LPG cylinders is hovering at about ₹200 per cylinder. Thus, the latest hike potentially tries to somewhat compensate for that amount, although the proportionate sales of commercial LPG are much smaller [compared to the domestic variant]. I would not read much into it,” Mr. Vashisht said.
Manpreet Singh, treasurer at the National Restaurants Association of India (NRAI), told The Hindu that the hike is nearly negligible, but that it prompted concerns that prices could increase further.
“Today’s hike in itself is negligible. The concerns are primarily about there being potential hikes in future," he said, adding, “This could increase the overall operating cost for restaurants coinciding with food inflation, which would increase the burden.”
The hike in commercial LPG prices came after two successive months wherein prices slipped by a total of about ₹380 per cylinder. This was after prices had spiralled upwards cumulatively by about ₹1,345 per cylinder across four tranches at the peak of the West Asia crisis.
Published - September 01, 2026 09:09 am IST

stories.headline: Alcaraz shines on return, Sabalenka begins U.S. Open 'three-peat' bid with win
stories.deck: Former champion Iga Swiatek and last year's runner-up Amanda Anisimova also advanced with impressive victories while Stefanos Tsitsipas served up an upset by knocking out 10th seed Arthur Fils on a sunny afternoon in New York.
stories.bodyText:
Defending champion Carlos Alcaraz won his first singles match in 139 days, while Aryna Sabalenka got her bid for a third straight U.S. Open title off to a winning start on Monday to light up the second day of the year's final Grand Slam.
Former champion Iga Swiatek and last year's runner-up Amanda Anisimova also advanced with impressive victories while Stefanos Tsitsipas served up an upset by knocking out 10th seed Arthur Fils on a sunny afternoon in New York.
Alcaraz's condition was one of the tournament's biggest question marks after his long spell out due to a wrist injury but the Spaniard enjoyed a comfortable return to action with a 6-4 6-4 6-4 win over Russian Roman Safiullin.
"You don't know what's going to happen in the match after 4-1/2 months almost. You don't know what's going to happen in your body, in your mind, everything. It's totally different," Alcaraz told reporters.
"But I just tried to play one game at a time and tried to feel good, to enjoy playing points, feeling the love from the people. Hopefully they enjoyed it."
The second seed's win ensured some star power remained in the men's field.
Novak Djokovic's shock defeat on Sunday left another hole in a men's draw already without injured world number one Jannik Sinner.
Sabalenka, Anisimova win easy
Earlier at Arthur Ashe Stadium, Sabalenka looked on her way to ending a frustrating patch of poor form with a 6-2 6-4 win over Colombia's Camila Osorio that earned her a clash with Russian Polina Iatcenko in the second round.
"I'm happy with my performance," said Sabalenka, who has not reached a title match since triumphing at Indian Wells and Miami to complete the 'Sunshine Double' in March.
"She's a tough opponent, makes you work really hard to get every point."
American Anisimova, whom Sabalenka beat in the final last year, got her campaign off to a good start on her 25th birthday with a 6-1 6-3 win over compatriot Ashlyn Krueger at Louis Armstrong Stadium.
Greece's Tsitsipas upset Cincinnati winner Fils 4-6 7-6(3) 6-1 6-4 in an early match on the same court, booking a second-round meeting with South African Lloyd Harris.
"It's very easy to not feel confident, especially when you haven't beaten top players in a long time," Tsitsipas said. "I'm ecstatic about today. It's an important, good victory for me, for my confidence."
Muchova, Noskova go through
Seven matches that were suspended on the outer courts on Sunday due to rain resumed on Monday, as organisers benefited from the extended three-day first-round schedule after expanding the main draw to 15 days in 2025.
Wimbledon finalist Karolina Muchova got the day underway on the Grandstand with a routine 6-3 6-0 win over Sinja Kraus and the Czech seventh seed plays Briton Katie Boulter next.
Linda Noskova, who defeated compatriot Muchova in the All England Club final, downed American Katie Volynets 7-5 6-1 to stay on track for back-to-back major titles.
It was a good day for the Americans on the largest of the outdoor courts. Emma Navarro ground out a 7-6(6) 6-7(1) 6-3 win over Frenchwoman Lois Boisson, while Taylor Townsend defeated Poland's Maja Chwalinska 6-2 6-3.
China's Olympic champion Zheng Qinwen, who was forced to go through qualifying only two years after reaching the quarter-finals in New York, beat Kristina Liutova 4-6 6-3 6-1.
Zheng's progress has stalled and her ranking has plummeted since an elbow injury forced her to undergo surgery last year.
Polish eighth seed Swiatek, the 2022 champion, beat China's Wang Xiyu 6-2 6-3 to kick off the night session on the second showcourt.
Another former winner, Stan Wawrinka, fell to Italy's Matteo Berrettini 7-6(4) 7-6(3) 6-0. The 41-year-old Swiss bid goodbye to the Grand Slam for the final time before his retirement at the end of the season.
Home hope Ben Shelton overcame Dutchman Tallon Griekspoor 1-6 6-1 7-6(3) 6-2 before Frances Tiafoe prevailed 6-4 4-6 3-6 6-3 6-4 in an all-American clash with Martin Damm.
Naomi Osaka unveiled another bold Grand Slam walk-on outfit before showing plenty of fight for a 7-6(6) 7-6(3) victory over unseeded Russian Anastasia Zakharova in a late-finishing match.

stories.headline: Konstas, Handscomb, Richardson picked for Australia A tour of India
stories.deck: Cricket Australia’s (CA) National Selection Panel said the tour holds great importance as it looks to expose players to subcontinental conditions and prepare them for the challenges of playing in India.
stories.bodyText:
Australia on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) named a 14-member squad, featuring several players with senior international experience, including pacer Ben Dwarshuis, Sam Konstas and Nathan McSweeney, for their series against India A in Puducherry later this month.
Cricket Australia’s (CA) National Selection Panel said the tour holds great importance as it looks to expose players to subcontinental conditions and prepare them for the challenges of playing in India.
A stand out performance in the red ball series will make a strong case for selection in the five Tests in India early next year.
Australia A will play two four-day matches and three one-day games, all in Puducherry. The first four-day game will begin on September 22, with the second unofficial Test scheduled to start on September 29.
The unofficial ODIs will be played on October 6, 9 and 11.
CA chairman George Bailey said the tour was particularly important with the senior Australian team set to tour India next year.
“We are excited by these squads and what they might achieve out of the series. Many of these players have played international cricket, whilst for others it’s a continuation of previous opportunities across Australia A and CAXI formats," said Bailey.
Peter Handscomb, Brendan Doggett, Konstas, McSweeney, Jhye Richardson and Todd Murphy have all played Test and international cricket while Mitch Owen, Jack Edwards, Tanveer Sangha, Liam Scott, Spencer Johnson, Ben Dwarshuis, Josh Phillipe, Aaron Hardie, Nikhil Chaudhary and Mahli Beardman have played in ODI or T20 Internationals.
“We consider these tours an important part of performance and developing game styles in sub-continent conditions as part of our continued investment into the Australia A program.

stories.headline: Pretorius stars as South Africa beat Zimbabwe again to strengthen tri-series campaign
stories.deck: South Africa emerged victorious in the Namibia T20I Tri-Series, defeating Zimbabwe by 43 runs. Lhuan-dre Pretorius's stellar performance, highlighted by a career-best 94, propelled the Proteas to a total of 185 for 7. Zimbabwe's batting lineup faltered under the pressure, with Bjorn Fortuin and Duan Jansen sharing seven wickets, ensuring the opposition was bowled out for just 142, and showcasing…
stories.bodyText:
South Africa continued their strong run in the Namibia T20I Tri-Series with another convincing victory over Zimbabwe, securing a comfortable 43-run win in the fourth match at the Namibia Cricket Ground on Tuesday.
Lhuan-dre Pretorius narrowly missed out on a maiden T20I century but produced a career-best 94 to set up South Africa’s second victory over Zimbabwe in the tournament. The opener’s sensational knock came off just 51 balls and featured 12 fours and three sixes.
Pretorius was named Player of the Match after helping South Africa post 185/7 before their bowlers completed the job by dismissing Zimbabwe for 142 in 17.4 overs.
Pretorius powers South Africa to 185
Put into bat, South Africa made an aggressive start, with Pretorius anchoring the innings and playing a key role in two partnerships of more than 50 runs for the first two wickets.
He found an able partner in Dewald Brevis, who struck 41 off 27 balls, as the Proteas built a strong platform. Zimbabwe did manage to fight back with regular wickets towards the latter stages, but South Africa had already done enough damage to reach a competitive 185/7.
Pretorius fell six runs short of a century, but the opener insisted the team victory mattered more than his individual milestone.
“Yeah, that's fine. I'm just glad we got over the line. Milestones will come and go, and yeah, it wasn't meant to be today, but I was just glad because we said at the 14-over mark we wanted to get to 200, and I knew if I got the team to 200 I'd get to the milestone. But yeah, I think milestones come and go, and today was not meant to be, but we won, so it's good,” Pretorius said.
Jansen, Fortuin dismantle Zimbabwe chase
Zimbabwe needed 186 for victory but struggled to maintain momentum after a promising beginning from Brian Bennett.
Their powerplay was derailed by a double-wicket maiden from captain 
Bjorn Fortuin
, and South Africa struck again soon after the fielding restrictions ended.
Duan Jansen produced a decisive burst, taking three wickets in four balls across two overs to leave Zimbabwe in serious trouble.
Captain Sikandar Raza offered some resistance with 45 off 33 balls, while Newman Nyamhuri added 27 with some aggressive hitting. But the pair could only reduce the eventual margin of defeat as Zimbabwe were bowled out for 142.
Fortuin was the standout bowler, finishing with 4/24 from 3.4 overs, while Jansen claimed 3/21. The pair shared seven wickets between them as South Africa repeatedly struck at crucial moments.
The result gives South Africa their second win over Zimbabwe in the tri-series, with Pretorius’ near-century and a disciplined bowling performance combining to secure another comprehensive victory.

stories.headline: Vice-captain Sooryavanshi shines as East beat Central to reach Duleep Trophy final
stories.deck: East Zone secured a place in the Duleep Trophy final with a four-wicket victory over Central Zone. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's aggressive cameo provided crucial momentum during the chase for East Zone. Mohammed Shami and Mukesh Kumar delivered fiery spells to dismantle Central Zone's batting lineup. Mukesh was named Player of the Match for his outstanding seven-wicket haul in the semifinal.
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s aggressive cameo, backed by fiery spells from 
Mohammed Shami
 and 
Mukesh Kumar
, helped East Zone storm into the Duleep Trophy final with a four-wicket win over defending champions Central Zone on Tuesday.
The 15-year-old Sooryavanshi made a valuable contribution of 40 off 43 balls as East Zone chased down a target of 159 on a turning pitch on the third day of the semifinal.
East, winners of the tournament in the 2012-13 season, will face either South Zone or North Zone in the final at Chepauk from September 6.
Sooryavanshi provides early spark before dramatic dismissal
Chasing 159, East needed a steady start as the pitch increasingly aided the spinners. Sooryavanshi initially adopted a cautious approach, scoring his first 15 runs from 30 balls.
But once he found his rhythm, the left-hander shifted gears spectacularly. His next 25 runs came from just 13 deliveries, featuring another six and three boundaries.
His opening partner 
Abhimanyu Easwaran
 was more fluent initially, including a six off off-spinner Saransh Jain over long-on, while Sooryavanshi struggled to find the same freedom against spin.
The teenager, however, came alive when Yash Thakur was introduced into the attack. 
Having already hammered the pacer for four fours and two sixes in the first innings, Sooryavanshi again went after him, smashing three fours and a six in the 14th over.
But his attacking approach also brought about his downfall. Sooryavanshi fell in the same over when Rajat Patidar completed a stunning running catch off Thakur.
His dismissal suddenly changed the mood of the chase, with East losing wickets at regular intervals. Harsh Dubey then struck twice in successive deliveries, removing Kumar Kushagra and Anukul Roy to leave East at 124 for five.
Shami, Mukesh dismantle Central before Kishan finishes chase
Earlier, Central resumed their second innings at 45 for three but suffered a dramatic collapse in the extended first session. They lost their remaining seven wickets to be bowled out for 158.
Shami and Mukesh were the chief destroyers, exploiting variable bounce and the assistance available to the bowlers. Shami finished with 3/56, while Mukesh claimed 4/44 to complete a seven-wicket haul in the match.
Mukesh was subsequently named Player of the Match, providing a timely boost to the India seamer who has been out of favour.
Central briefly threatened to stretch the chase when Dubey and Arshad Khan added 43 for the ninth wicket, taking their side beyond 150. But East held their nerve to complete the victory.
Ishan Kishan then produced a composed 39 not out from 41 balls to guide East home with minimal further trouble.
“For a personal point of view, and not only me, the entire team members are looking forward to playing in the final. It will be heartening if we can go on and win that title,” Easwaran said after the match.

briefs.headline: National Youth Championships: Tamil Nadu’s sprinters shine
briefs.deck: Promising sprinter Neil Samraj R of Tamil Nadu dominated the men’s 100m dash. His winning time of 10.46 seconds was better than the previous youth national record of 10.63 seconds set by Anshu Rajak in 2023 in Coimbatore
briefs.bodyText:
Tamil Nadu sprinters shone on the opening day of the National Youth Athletics Championships as they won the 100m gold in both the men's and women's sections on Tuesday (September 1, 2026).
Promising sprinter Neil Samraj R of Tamil Nadu dominated the men’s 100m dash. His winning time of 10.46 seconds was better than the previous youth national record of 10.63 seconds set by Anshu Rajak in 2023 in Coimbatore.
Tamil Nadu’s T Mrithika claimed the women's 100m gold medal, clocking 11.78 seconds, bettering the previous meet record of 11.80 seconds set by Dutee Chand in 2012 in Bengaluru.
Mrithika was the only sprinter in the final to break the 12-second barrier.
Suchithra S of Karnataka edged past Saawari Kulkarni (Maharashtra) to win the silver with a time of 12.03 seconds. Saawari clocked 12.09 seconds for the bronze.

briefs.deck: With the Men in Blue heading to Japan to defend their Asian Games gold later this month, they may look to tread cautiously with their pace spearhead
briefs.bodyText:
Sanju Samson has returned to India’s T20I squad for three matches against Afghanistan at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi from September 13 to 17. briefs.headline: The FIFA World Cup deserved Lionel Messi
briefs.bodyText:
On the grandest of all stages, Lionel Messi conjured up an act of magic for ages. How he won Argentina the World Cup in 2022 will remain one of the greatest stories in sport.
He scored two goals in the final against France in what many regard as the finest World Cup game of all time. That was the game in which Kylian Mbappe performed an unforgettable hat-trick. Only Messi could have made the young Frenchman look the second best on that night in Doha.
That final, which ended 3-3 after extra time and thus went into the shootout, was watched by about 1.5 billion people across the world. Those fans would have felt the match, and the World Cup, was Argentina’s when they saw Messi’s men go 2-0 up after 36 minutes. He had opened the scoring from the penalty spot and Angel Di Maria netted the second. The Argentines had that two-goal lead late into the game, till the 80th minute. But within a space of a couple of minutes, Mbappe scored twice to force extra time. Messi, though, made it 3-2 with 12 minutes remaining.
Mbappe, however, converted the penalty to pave the way for more penalties.
In the shootout, Messi and Mbappe took the first kicks for their teams, and scored, too. But, the misses from Kingsley Coman and Aurelien Tchouameni proved costly for France.
It was only fitting though that Argentina triumphed.
The planet’s most beautiful player deserved to win the biggest prize in the beautiful game. It would have been a great injustice if Messi hadn’t got that opportunity to have that memorable stolen kiss on the trophy. At that time, it wasn’t sure if the living legend would be around for another World Cup.
He stamped his authority on that World Cup in a manner only the most gifted could have. He delivered when his team wanted. And he did it with a touch of genius. Remember how he set up that goal for Julian Alvarez in the semifinal against Croatia?
Qatar 2022 will forever be a classic example of a rare genius at work, and under tremendous pressure.

briefs.headline: Delhi HC issues notice on plea seeking policy for women athletes returning after maternity
briefs.deck: The petition by wrestler Vinesh Phogat seeks a framework to facilitate the return of women athletes to competitive sports after pregnancy and maternity leave
briefs.bodyText:
The Delhi High Court on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) sought the response of the Centre, the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) and the Indian Olympic Association on a petition by wrestler Vinesh Phogat, seeking a structured framework to facilitate the return of women athletes to competitive sports after pregnancy and maternity leave.
Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma issued the notice on the plea and listed the matter for further hearing on November 18.
Senior advocate Rajshekhar Rao, appearing for Ms. Phogat, said: “This is a larger question on lady athletes and maternity leave and impact on their ability to participate in the sport”. Mr. Rao pointed out that international standards provide certain benefits and protection of rankings to athletes who take maternity leave.
In the plea, Ms. Phogat sought directions for the formulation of a fair and structured framework for women athletes returning from maternity, transparent and objectively verifiable selection and nomination processes, as well as an alternative mechanism for athletes disadvantaged by maternity-related absences.
Ms. Phogat, who gave birth to a child in July 2025, has contended that after resuming her wrestling career, she was required to re-enter the competitive pathway without any accommodations for the period during which she could not compete due to maternity.
According to the plea, the eligibility criteria relied on performances in tournaments held during her maternity period, effectively penalising her for an absence over which she had no control, instead of providing an alternative route for her return to competition.
Challenges WFI notice
Ms. Phogat has also challenged two show-cause notices issued by the WFI and the disciplinary proceedings initiated against her.
The court asked the WFI’s counsel to obtain instructions on the matter and listed the challenge to the notices for hearing on September 29.
WFI’s counsel submitted that the federation had given Ms. Phogat two opportunities for a hearing but there had been “no show”. A final opportunity had now been granted and the hearing was scheduled for September 2, the counsel said.

briefs.headline: Asian Games cricket row: Japan Cricket CEO says teams can make own arrangements
briefs.deck: Japan Cricket CEO Naoki Alex Miyaji clarified Asian Games accommodation arrangements for teams. Participating teams are offered hotel stays and can arrange their own lodging. Logistical constraints are affecting many sports, not just cricket at the event. The Korogi Sports Park venue was built from scratch within a tight timeframe. Organisers are confident cricket will make a strong impression at…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: With concerns over accommodation and other logistical arrangements emerging ahead of cricket’s return to the 
Asian Games
, Japan Cricket Association (JCA) CEO Naoki Alex Miyaji has sought to put the apprehensions into perspective, saying participating teams have been offered hotel accommodation but are free to make their own arrangements.
At a recent Asian Cricket Council (ACC) meeting, leading cricketing nations reportedly raised concerns over the accommodation arrangements, with the designated hotel located around 20km from the Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin City, Aichi Prefecture, where the cricket matches will be held.
The Asian Games begin on September 17.
Japan Cricket CEO clarifies accommodation arrangements
Miyaji stressed that the JCA is playing a limited role in the event’s organisation.
“The Asian Games is being organised by the organising committee Aichi-Nagoya Games Organizing Committee (AINAGOC) in collaboration with the ACC under the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA),” Miyaji told PTI.
“The JCA has provided support in some areas but is not directly involved so I am not able to directly answer all of your questions. What I can say is that all parties are working hard to ensure the success of Cricket in the Asian Games.
“I can also assure you that the ACC have been discussing accommodation options with AINAGOC for a long time. The participating teams in cricket are being offered hotel accommodation,” he said.
Miyaji also pointed out that cricket is not the only sport facing logistical constraints at the Games.
“Many other sports are being accommodated in much more limited facilities such as a cruise ship or container hotels. The teams are free to arrange their own accommodation if they chose to do so,” he said.
‘Toilets will be available within the player area’
Miyaji also sought to allay concerns over reports that team washrooms could be located at least half a kilometre from the playing arena.
“Please note that toilets will be available within the player area. There are both temporary and permanent facilities at the venue. The facilities on the ground are temporary, but AINAGOC have worked very closely with the ACC for over a year now to ensure that the best facilities are provided within the limited timeline and facility restrictions,” Miyaji said.
He also addressed concerns over the makeshift dressing rooms being prepared for the tournament.
“Despite being temporary, the facilities will provide as comfortable a space as possible for the players and officials. There are also permanent facilities around the ground which will be available to the players,” he said.
Korogi Sports Park built from scratch
Miyaji explained that organisers had only 17 months to prepare the venue, which had to be developed from scratch because Aichi Prefecture did not have an established cricket facility.
“They only had 17 months to prepare and had to start from scratch as there were no Cricket venues of any standard in Aichi Prefecture. Considering the limited time and resources available, AINAGOC and ACC have worked together to ensure that the playing facilities are suitable,” he said.
Sri Lanka Cricket has also provided curators to work on the turf and hybrid pitches.
“It will be a full size ground with turf and hybrid pitches prepared by the best curators which Sri Lanka Cricket should be credited for providing,” Miyaji said.
“There are limits on what they can do within these tight limits, but from what I have seen, the playing surface and field will be the best seen in Cricket's inclusion in the Asian Games.”
The JCA, meanwhile, has concentrated largely on building local interest in the sport.
“We have taken cricket to many school and shopping centres which have received great enthusiasm. Thanks to the full support of Nisshin City, we are confident that the local community will be 100% behind the Asian Games.”
Miyaji remained confident that cricket would make a strong impression when the continental event is staged in Japan.
“Cricket will be one of the largest sports in the Asian Games. It will also be the first time the top Cricket teams of Asia will be playing in Japan,” he added.

briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: 
Krunal Pandya
 has hinted that his hopes of returning to international cricket remain alive after the all-rounder was left out of India’s squad for the upcoming three-match T20I series against Afghanistan.
Shortly after 
the squad was announced on Tuesday
, Krunal shared a poignant message on social media, writing: “Hope is still alive”.
The 35-year-old left-arm spinner has been pushing for a return to India’s T20I setup and, as reported earlier by TimesofIndia.com, had emerged as an option for the selectors following India’s recent outings in Ireland and England.
Afghanistan will host India for three T20Is in New Delhi on September 13, 15 and 17, with the Arun Jaitley Stadium set to stage all three matches.
Krunal misses out despite strong IPL season
Krunal last played for India in the 2021 T20I series against Sri Lanka but has remained on the selectors’ radar following an impressive IPL 2026 campaign.
Playing for Royal Challengers Bengaluru, Krunal picked up 14 wickets during the season and once again showcased his value as a left-arm spin-bowling all-rounder.
India have been exploring options in that department after their recent T20I assignments. Axar Patel featured in all seven matches against Ireland and England, but managed only four wickets — two in the two T20Is against Ireland and two in four games against England.
The selectors opted against recalling him for the Afghanistan series.
His social media message suggests he remains hopeful of another opportunity with India.
Bumrah returns, several players subject to fitness
Pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah has returned to the squad for the Afghanistan series, although his selection is subject to fitness clearance.
Bumrah had been sidelined after sustaining an impact injury to his knee during India’s ODI series in England. He subsequently missed the two-Test series in Sri Lanka after being advised rest by the 
BCCI
 medical team.
Nitish Kumar Reddy, Washington Sundar and Harshit Rana have also been included subject to fitness clearance. All three have recently dealt with injuries and are currently under Return to Play protocols.
Rana suffered a Grade 1 hamstring injury during India’s third T20I against England, while Washington sustained a hamstring injury during the third ODI against England. Reddy had also been recovering from an injury that ruled him out of India’s recent assignments.
As reported earlier by TimesofIndia.com, Hardik Pandya has also missed out after a late leg niggle disrupted his comeback plans at the BCCI Centre of Excellence. He has not played competitive cricket since turning out for Mumbai Indians on May 24, while his last appearance for India came in the T20 World Cup final on March 8.

briefs.headline: ‘I felt great’: Alcaraz makes stunning US Open return after 139 days out with injury
briefs.deck: Carlos Alcaraz returned to tennis after a long injury layoff. He played his first match in 139 days at the US Open. Alcaraz secured a convincing victory against Roman Safiullin in straight sets. The young Spaniard confirmed he was playing pain-free and felt great. He expressed happiness and a desire to enjoy every match.
briefs.bodyText:
NEW YORK CITY: For two hours and 21-minutes on Arthur Ashe, Carlos Alcaraz’s game answered the big question that had accompanied his much-anticipated return to tennis.
The 23-year-old Spaniard, playing his first match in 139 days after a wrist injury in mid-April, faced Russia’s Roman Safiullin in the US Open. He pummelled the ball, pulled off impossible gets and picked up shots off his shoelaces, turning defence into delicate winners on his way to a convincing 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 win.
Alcaraz opened his final service game with a volley winner, caressed inches above the ground, then turned to the crowd, calling for some love, hand on his ear. The spectators roared and Alcaraz’ smile sparked the sun.
The second seed underlined that he was playing pain-free.
“I felt great. I don’t know how it looked from outside, but from inside, my feeling was that I was hitting the ball normal. I was playing pretty normal, playing my style, and the wrist felt great. I'm going to still take care of it, obviously, I'm just really happy it's pain-free finally,” he told international media.
The defending champion arrived on court in a dark-brown, almost espresso, ensemble, the fashion world’s warmer alternative to black. 
Alcaraz shed his overshirt to reveal an oversized ombré sleeveless tank, paired with matching brown shorts edged in a thick white trim. A narrow hairband held his unruly mop in place. A white compression sleeve covered the precautionary taping on his wrist.
In a match of small margins, where Alcaraz, it appeared was doing just enough, he hit 28 winners, 20 of them off the forehand. He faced six breakpoints, with Safiullin converting just one. The 23-year-old converted four of the seven break points he earned, a difference that proved decisive.
The second seed teed off on his returns, but was more controlled with his serve. Alcaraz, who enjoys amping up the speed upwards of 130 mph, hit a top speed of 128 in the first-round match. The average speed on his first and second serves was 113 and 97 respectively.
“The serve is the shot that I was struggling the most,” he said, adding, “There are some players who like to return serves coming at 130 miles and when you serve a little bit slower they struggle a little bit. So most of that speed (generated) is because of him (opponent). It was kind of tactics.”
“I just always struggle with the serve, but it will be back, for sure,” he said.
For the seven-time major winner, who faces 23-year-old Jaime Faria of Portugal in the second round on Tuesday, the biggest shift was perhaps mental.
“It was a difficult day for me, but at the same time, a really beautiful day,” he said. “I was really nervous. Really, really nervous, but also just happy, because, for me, my goal here is to compete, to enjoy, and let's see how my body's going to react after the matches.”
Alcaraz explained, “I had forgotten how a match day feels like. I was warming up, and I don't remember actually what I used to do, in the warm-up. So to kind of get that feeling again. That's why I was really nervous, because kind of I just forgot the competition.”
“I don't know how far I'm going to go in the tournament,” he admitted, “But what I just really want to do is enjoy every time that I'm going to walk into the court, feeling the energy from the people, feeling the competition. That's why I enjoyed so much today.”
